Myrtille, an open source project to connect remote desktops from a simple browser

Myrtille is a simple way to connect remote desktops from a web browser.

As a web UI, it’s device and OS independant. Server side, it uses the .NET (C#) framework and the RDP protocol through an HTTP gateway.

It supports HTML4 and HTML5, file transfer and WebP compression.

More information at http://cedrozor.github.io/myrtille/

Feedback is welcome! :)

I'm a little weary. I'm assuming there's protections to make sure it those running the server can't get in to my system? Not sure end to end encryption would help, as they're the ones in control of both ends if it's web based.

Hi, Myrtille is just an HTML4 and 5 client (viewer) for an RDP connection. It's exactly the same thing as the Windows based rdp client (mstsc.exe), except it's browser based.

Once you are connected to the server with your credentials (user name and password), you have indeed access to the system if your account have enough privileges. These can be controlled by using Group Policies Objects, linked or not to an Active Directory if the computer is in a domain.

End to end encryption, though https or wss (secure websockets), have nothing to do with it... it would just avoid prying eyes.

What I meant is:

Unless I'm portfordwarding, the handshake is through a 3rd party server. How do I know the server isn't keylogging whatever else they could be doing.

Myrtille isn't a public remote desktop gateway like some exist on the internet (and are not open sourced); you have to install it on a private server, that you control. The same question could be asked if you use a public proxy... that's why it's always better to use encryption anyway.
